subject: Discovery recap — multi-tenancy controls and per-customer routing
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Walker <jordan.walker@acme-retail.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap — multi-tenancy controls and per-customer routing

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our discovery on multi-tenant controls and routing for Acme Retail's LLM usage:

Pain points:
- Promotion-driven traffic spikes from specific tenants cause rate/overage issues and inconsistent latency.
- No per-customer quotas or token-level throttles today; current API gateway only supports coarse limits.
- Need ability to route high-tier customers to dedicated model variants/pools for better latency and quality.

Current stack:
- GCP-hosted microservices behind an API gateway (internal). Models are currently proxied to a shared endpoint.
- Usage tracked in BigQuery; billing reconciled monthly.

Success criteria for a pilot:
- Per-tenant rate limits (tokens/sec and daily quota) enforced at request time.
- Per-tenant routing/policy to allow tiering (e.g., top 5 tenants -> dedicated pool, others -> shared). 
- Observable per-tenant cost + latency reporting (token-level telemetry) to correlate cost to revenue.
- Maintain p95 latency <200ms for top-tier tenants under normal load.

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to share two implementation options: a) Gateway-side rate-limiting + tagging + shared pool; b) Dedicated pool + routing + burst allowances for VIPs. Attached draft: rate-limits-options.pdf and example-config.yaml.
2) Technical deep-dive with Monica (solutions engineer) to scope SOW & pilot timeline — propose 60-minute session next week.
3) Acme to confirm pilot tenant list (suggest 5 top tenants) and any compliance docs required.

If that matches your notes, we'll schedule the deep-dive and circulate a short SOW.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

Attachments: rate-limits-options.pdf (summary of approaches), example-config.yaml (example routing + quota rules)

From: Jordan Walker <jordan.walker@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — multi-tenancy controls and per-customer routing

Thanks Dylan — this is great and aligns with what we discussed.

A few clarifications / confirmations:
- Promotions are the primary cause of spikes; we see 3–4x baseline traffic for a subset of tenants during campaigns.
- We currently cannot route to different model variants per tenant — that would be a big win.
- Success criteria: p95 <200ms for VIPs, visibility into per-tenant cost. Cost target is ~$0.50 per 1k tokens for shared workloads (open to dedicated pricing for VIPs).

We can pilot with 5 tenants. Priya will share the list and a short security checklist; we do require SOC2 evidence and a VPC peering option if possible.

Available times for the deep-dive next week: Tue 6/15 10–12 PT or Wed 6/16 14–16 PT.

Thanks,

Jordan
Jordan Walker
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
